events.summary:
At 313 AM CDT, trained weather spotters reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches
of rain have fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but no
additional rainfall is expected. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported. City of Aberdeen employee reports
vehicles stalled due to water and multiple streets
completely underwater, at least a foot deep.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Aberdeen and Bath.

events.summary:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 1 PM TO 8 PM MDT THIS AFTERNOON
FOR SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS FOR IDAHO FIRE WEATHER ZONE 427...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 427 Goose Creek and Raft
River Valley/Southern Sawtooth NF/Twin Falls BLM south of the
Snake River.

* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected to
develop Tuesday. Lightning may generate new fire starts. New
starts may spread rapidly.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Both wet and dry thunderstorms expected with
25 to 35 percent coverage.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusts of 30 to 40 mph are possible.

events.region: Northern Seward Peninsula; Upper Kobuk Valleys; Lower Koyukuk Valley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* AFFECTED AREA...Northern Seward Peninsula, Upper Kobuk Valleys
and Lower Koyukuk Valley.

* TIMING...From 10 AM AKDT Wednesday through Wednesday evening.

* THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE INDEX...Scattered in the Kobuk and Lower
Koyukuk. Isolated in the northern Seward Peninsula.

* WINDS...North 5 to 10 mph.

* HUMIDITY...As low as 38 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Lows in the mid 40s. Highs in the lower 80s.

* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected due to
scattered thunderstorms. Thunderstorms will come with frequent
lightning and outflow boundaries. Any lightning can cause new
ignitions since the fuels are dry and burnable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop
in the Upper Kobuk and Lower Koyukuk Valleys. Sea breezes Wednesday afternoon
will likely limit thunderstorm potential along the coast

events.summary:
* AFFECTED AREA...Lower Kobuk Valley.

* TIMING...From 10 AM AKDT Wednesday through Wednesday evening.

* THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE INDEX...Isolated to Scattered.

* WINDS...West 5 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph.

* HUMIDITY...As low as 42 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Highs in the upper 70s. Lows in the upper 40s.

* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are possible due to
scattered thunderstorms. Thunderstorms will come with frequent
lightning and outflow boundaries. Any lightning can cause new
ignitions since the fuels are dry and burnable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Westerly sea breezes Wednesday afternoon
will likely limit thunderstorm potential along the coast, with
more concern further east into the upper Kobuk.

events.region: Coastal waters from Cape Blanco OR to Pt. St. George CA out 10 nm; Waters from Cape Blanco OR to Pt. St. George CA from 10 to 60 nm
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...North winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and steep
wind-driven seas 6 to 7 ft through this morning. North winds
increase late this morning to 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 40
kt, and seas become very steep 8 to 11 ft.

* WHERE...Conditions hazardous to small craft are expected south
of Cape Blanco, with very steep and hazardous seas developing
south of Gold Beach and beyond 5 nm from shore today into
Thursday.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 5 AM PDT Friday.
For the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 11 AM this morning to 5
AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Bar crossings will become especially
treacherous.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks
